subject: pack.t is INVISIBLE to the sweep gate: 0 baseline rows because it always TIMEOUTs
description:
DONE s322. Measurement fix shipped: sweep-perl-tests.pl retries a TIMEOUT once at 3x the timeout at the END of the queue (--no-retry disables); both inverse guards probed (still-too-slow retries exactly once and lands TIMEOUT; --no-retry restores the single attempt).

MEASURED s322: pack.t times out at 90s, retries at 270s, completes in 166s -> 5636 pass / 89 fail, and those failures are IDENTICAL to the blessed baseline (52 unique descriptions both sides) -> sweep-diff 0 new / 0 fixed.

PREMISE CORRECTION: the task's original claim "0 baseline rows" was FALSE. docs/fail-baseline.tsv has always carried 58 pack.t rows; the claim came from grepping a TSV that contains NUL bytes, which makes grep treat the file as binary and print nothing. The real hole was narrower but still real: a timing-out file's baseline rows are reported "DID NOT RUN - unverified", so a regression inside it is invisible while the headline still reads "0 new". That hole is now closed.

Nothing left to bless post-R1 (Fable's step 2 is moot - the rows were already blessed). What remains is ordinary near-green triage of those 52 known failures, and the separate slowdown task #184.
